text: Compute the modular data of (M_T, Omega) on the vacuum, one- and two-particle spaces: Delta^{it} = U(0, -2 pi t) and J_{M_T} = J on H_0 + H_1 + H_2
Build n-particle vectors as products of the fields chi(xi), chi'(eta) applied to Omega and prove the Tomita relation inductively in the particle number k
Apply the Buchholz-Lechner / Alazzawi-Lechner Bisognano-Wichmann theorem for wedge-local fields
Apply Mund's theorem that Bisognano-Wichmann follows from the particle structure of a local net
Prove the Haag-Ruelle out-states at level n are sqrt(n!) P_n(slowest x ... x fastest) for all n, identifying the scattering states
Verify the formal Tomita identity S_M = S_0 numerically at particle degrees 4 and 5
V(t) = U(0, -2 pi t) Delta_{M_T}^{-it} and I = J_{M_T} J act as the identity on every vector of H
The standard subspace of M_T is contained in the free standard subspace H_0, equivalently {S_M = S_0} is dense
Bisognano-Wichmann holds on the closed span of all scattering states and that span is all of H
Modular nuclearity of the map M_T(x) -> Delta^{1/4} M Omega holds for all wedge translations x
